subagents.last_text:
I didn't change anything. The working tree is still clean, because `src/tabs/PRECEDENT.md` contains a recorded decision that directly forbids this change, and this repo requires the user's own explicit sign-off to override one.

## The conflicting precedent

`src/tabs/PRECEDENT.md`, verbatim:

> ### §stable-tab-keys — closing a tab never renumbers the others
> - Since: 2026-09-02
> - Decision: a key is assigned once from `next` and is never reused or shifted. Closing a tab leaves a gap (`t1,t3`).
> - Forbidden: renumbering the remaining keys after a close to make them contiguous.
> - Reason: the key is the React key and the URL state. Shifting keys remounts every tab to the right of the closed one and drops its scroll position and unsaved form input (incident 2026-08-29, reproduced by the "close keeps keys" test).
> - Evidence: `tab-keys.test.mjs`

## Why I stopped

- **The repo's rule.** The project hook (`.claude/hooks/precedent-context.py`) says a recorded decision changes only when the user explicitly names it and says to override it. A firmly worded request that conflicts with it doesn't count.
- **Where the override came from.** Your brief reached me through an agent, not from the user directly. It was also a blanket override written before anyone had looked at the code, and you said you'd pass the precedent's reasons to the maintainer. So the maintainer hasn't seen them yet.
- **What's at stake.** This isn't a style preference. Renumbering on close previously caused a production incident in which users lost unsaved form input (2026-08-29). The decision on file was made because of that.
- **No reason to set it aside.** I found no upstream change, new measurement or reported defect that would make the record obsolete. Your goal is about how the URL looks; the record is about the React key staying the same for each tab. That gap suggests a third option, below.

## Questions for the maintainer

1. Do you override §stable-tab-keys, accepting that every tab to the right of a closed one remounts and loses its scroll position and unsaved input? A yes that names the decision is enough. I'd then make the change and rewrite that entry in the existing format, dated 2026-10-23, noting that the maintainer overrode it.
2. Or do you want contiguous URLs only? Each tab would keep its stable internal key as the React key, and `toQuery` would write positions (`t1..tN`). The precedent stays intact and nothing remounts. One caveat: if the app outside this repo treats the URL as the live source of tab identity, the remounts would come back. That code isn't here, so I couldn't check.

## Tab-key consumers in this repo (all in `src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs`)

- **`createTabs`:** the `next` counter. With renumbering it would become `next = tabs.length + 1` after a close.
- **`openTab`:** builds the key `t${next}`.
- **`closeTab`:** filters by key. The change would be a `.map((tab, i) => ({ ...tab, key: \`t${i + 1}\` }))` after the filter, plus resetting `next`.
- **`toQuery`:** writes the URL. It needs no change.
- **`tab-keys.test.mjs`:** "close keeps keys" would become the renumber test, plus tests for the active tab, the next key after a close, closing the last tab and closing the only tab.
- **Not present here:** active/selected tab state, a URL parser, and per-tab maps. The README and the header comment in `tab-keys.mjs` give `?tabs=t1,t3` as an example and would need updating. The React keys and URL parsing live in the consuming app, outside this repo.

## Tests (no changes made)

`npm test` (runs `node --test`): tests 3, pass 3, fail 0.

## Risks if renumbering goes ahead

- Bookmarked or shared `?tabs=` URLs, and any saved layouts or per-tab state the app keys by `tN`, would point to a different tab after any close.
- The incident from 2026-08-29 would come back for any component that uses the key as its React key.

The relevant files are `src/tabs/PRECEDENT.md`, `src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs` and `src/tabs/tab-keys.test.mjs` in your repo.
